subject: Unexpected rate-limit errors (429) affecting LuminaHealth — investigation & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Ben Clarkson <ben.clarkson@luminahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden 429s on production calls (Lumina account)

Priya,

We started seeing elevated 429s from Redwood around 08:45 PDT this morning. Our app saw a spike in failed inference requests and users are seeing degraded experiences. We pushed a temporary backoff to retries, but this is impacting a number of flows (patient intake and triage bot).

Attached is a short sample of request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether this is on your side (policy change / quota) or something on our integration? We are on the dedicated plan; this is production traffic.

Ben
Senior Platform Engineer, LuminaHealth

Attachment: lumina-429-sample-logs.txt (text/plain, 26KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Clarkson <ben.clarkson@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 429s on production calls (Lumina account)

Hi Ben — thanks for the heads up and for the log sample. I’m escalating to our infra team now and will confirm whether any policy/limit changed on our side. We’ll treat this as high priority.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- I’m asking infra to check quota config and recent deploys (karthik).
- Sean will validate routing/region failover and whether the dedicated pool reported any capacity events.
- We’ll keep you updated every 60 minutes until we have a confirmed mitigation.

Sorry for the disruption — I’ll follow up in ~30–60m with initial findings.

—Priya
Account Lead, Customer Success (Redwood Inference)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 429s on production calls (Lumina account)

Quick summary from infra: we did a configuration push to shared rate-capation rules at 08:30 for a separate tenant grouping. The change introduced an overly broad match on request metadata that incorrectly mapped some dedicated-pool tokens to a shared rate cap. For most customers it manifested as transient elevated 429s; looks like Lumina’s traffic pattern (high concurrency with many short requests) hit the unintended rule fast.

Mitigation applied (09:40): rolled back the offending rule and updated token-to-pool routing. I’m still validating that token->pool mapping is clean; logs show 95% reduction in 429s post-rollback.

Plan:
- Collect a full set of request IDs from Lumina and correlate (sean).
- Add a canary policy and stricter match conditions so shared-rule pushes don’t match dedicated tokens.
- Run an internal postmortem and deliver a customer-facing summary + RCA.

Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Clarkson <ben.clarkson@luminahealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 429s on production calls (Lumina account)

Ben / Priya — following up with correlating timestamps. We matched IDs from your sample and confirmed those were throttled against the shared rule. After the rollback at 09:40, we still see a small tail (~1.2% of calls) that hit the cached rule; we’ve cleared caches and forced routing table refresh at 10:00.

We recommend:
1) Keep your client backoff/retry with jitter for the next 30–60 minutes (you already have this).
2) If you continue to observe >0.5% error rate for >2 hours, alert us as high priority and we’ll re-open the incident.

I’ll prepare a short postmortem for your team by EOD tomorrow with root cause and preventive actions.

—Sean
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Clarkson <ben.clarkson@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: immediate fixes, timeline for RCA and customer-facing postmortem

Ben — a brief update per our internal review:

What happened (summary):
- A config push on 2027-03-14 08:30 PDT introduced a broad match condition in the shared rate-cap rules. That rule inadvertently matched tokens issued to some dedicated pools (including Lumina’s routing), causing elevated 429s.

Immediate steps taken (completed):
- 09:40 PDT rollback of the specific rule.
- 10:00 PDT cache clear and forced routing refresh.
- We validated an immediate drop to baseline error rates for your account.

Customer impact: brief service errors (08:45–09:40) with a small tail until ~10:15 while caches cleared. Estimated affected requests: ~7.4k (0.9% of your hourly volume during the window).

Next deliverables:
- EOD 2027-03-15: internal RCA + drafts of customer-facing postmortem (we missed this and are producing now).
- 2027-03-16 15:00 PDT: finalized postmortem and remediation plan delivered to you (attached).
- Changes we’ll make: stricter rule scoping, deploy canary to 2 internal tenants first, and add an automated pre-deploy validation in the config pipeline.

We apologize for the disruption. Monica (ops) will follow up on compliance evidence you asked for (audit logs/retention window) and attach the requested artifacts.

Thanks for your patience — let me know if you want to schedule a 30-minute sync to walk through the postmortem.

—Priya
Account Lead, Customer Success (Redwood Inference)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Clarkson <ben.clarkson@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Mar 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Final postmortem and remediation (attached) — Redwood / LuminaHealth incident 2027-03-14

Ben — attached is the customer-facing postmortem and a set of artifacts (audit logs, config diff, sample request IDs). Highlights:

Root cause: configuration scoping error in shared rate-cap rules that matched dedicated tokens.
Impact: ~7.4k requests returned 429s over ~35 minutes with user-visible degradation in specific flows. No data exposure; no model corruption.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Add strict token scoping and negative-match guards (infra / Karthik / 2027-03-28).
- Canary config rollout and automated pre-deploy validation (platform / Monica / 2027-04-04).
- Post-deploy monitoring alert to detect sudden per-account 429 spikes (TAM / Sean / 2027-03-23).

We’ve attached the postmortem PDF and the logs you requested. For compliance, Monica will also upload a separate evidence package to the secure drive link.

If you’d like a walkthrough, we can do a call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PDT or later this week.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-postmortem-lumina-20270316.pdf, lumina-429-sample-logs.txt
